newsitem.title: UK: HOT, DRY WEATHER SPEEDS SOUTH UK WHEAT HARVEST.
newsitem.headline: HOT, DRY WEATHER SPEEDS SOUTH UK WHEAT HARVEST.

text.p: Farmers in southern England moved fast to harvest wheat in hot sunny weather over the weekend, farming sources said.
Monday started warm and dry in most areas. But sporadic thunder showers were likely so farmers were keen to make as much progress as possible, they said.

Combine harvesters were out in force in the counties just to the north of London, while the past three days have seen the first cuts of wheat further to the north-east in the important grain producing region of East Anglia.
"There's been a lot going on in the last three or four days," one farming source in Norfolk said.
It had included the first wheat harvesting, with the weekend's hot, dry weather bringing some of the first wheat to the stage where it could be cut.
"The yields seem quite good," the source said, although no records were likely to be broken. There were more worries over quality, after the rain which affected the later stages of growth.
In the south-west of England, where heavy rain caused floods and brought harvesting to a halt early last week, there was still water on the ground in places.
But even there, farmers had been getting on with harvesting over the weekend, a spokesman for the National Farmers Union in the region said.
"The damage to yields (from the floods) shouldn't be too severe, but the quality probably will suffer," he said. "There's an awful lot of water still around."
